Akshay: Heads-up — saw a p99 latency jump on Dedicated after the v5.2 checkpoint onboarded this morning. Rolling deploy hit 2x p99 on long-tail rw workloads.
Lina: Oh no. Which pool/region?
Akshay: us-west-2:d-gpu-pool-7 primarily. Baseline p99 ~95ms -> 210ms. Throughput fine.
Jon: CI perf runner also red right?
ci-bot: perf-ci: build 2951234502 failed perf threshold: p99_latency increased by 112ms (threshold 50ms). See: https://ci/reports/2951234502
Maria: I started a quick profiler on a repro trace. Early signs look like KV cache eviction spike and kernel switch churn.
Akshay: I captured a short log snippet from the staging run:
```
2026-03-18T09:12:03Z INFO kernel-selector selected kernel: compute_fused_attn_qkv32
2026-03-18T09:12:03Z INFO kv-cache evictions: 0 -> 14 (window 30s)
2026-03-18T09:12:03Z INFO selected kernel: compute_fused_attn_qkv16 (fallback)
2026-03-18T09:12:04Z WARN batch-scheduler stragglers: 23/512
```
Lina: Kernel flip/flop plus eviction = more mem pressure -> higher tail. Any diff between v5.1 and v5.2 tokenization?
Maria: Yes — model team changed the tokenizer split on punctuation for that checkpoint (char-delim normalization tweak). We compared token counts over the eval prompts: median tokens +18%, 95p +40%.
Jon: That explains KV thrash. More tokens => larger KV maps and more frequent evictions, also batch shape distribution shifts kernel selector to smaller-kernel path.
Akshay: Bisecting the deploy chain now. Early hypothesis: tokenizer config change in the checkpoint plus kernel_selector heuristics exposed a corner we didn't handle (prefers qkv16 kernel when avg seq len >X).
Maria: Quick profiler flame graph shows hot path in kv-cache maintenance (serialize/deserialize) instead of attention compute.
Lina: Can you paste the kernel-selector decision trace?
Maria: Here (abbreviated):
```
input_len=256, batch_shape=[1,256], selector_score={qkv32: 0.42, qkv16:0.58}
fallbacks applied due to mem_estimate>pool_remaining -> choose qkv16
```
Akshay: Repro steps: onboard v5.2 to a staging pool with synthetic prompts that mimic the punctuation-heavy queries. Repro rate ~100% for p99 spike.
Jon: Immediate mitigation options: 1) revert the checkpoint rollout, 2) pin kernel selector to prefer qkv32 for this model, 3) increase KV alloc headroom on Dedicated (short-term).
Lina: We can't increase headroom for all customers. Revert + pin seems safest while infra analyzes.
sre-bot: Incident draft created: INC-2026-0318-01 (latency regression, dedicated pool).
Akshay: Started a revert PR for the onboard job (rolling back to v5.1) and a temp kernel selector override for v5.2 to force qkv32.
Maria: I'll run a targeted perf CI against the revert branch. If CI green -> cut revert.
Jon: For longer term: we should add token-length histogram telemetry to onboarding checks, and make kernel-selector aware of tokenization deltas between checkpoints.
Lina: Agreed. Also add a KV warmup / gradual ramp when median length jumps >15% during rollout.
Akshay: Filing follow-ups: onboarding-checks#122 (token-length gate), kernel-selector#378 (make selectors robust to sudden seq dist shifts), kv-cache#55 (auto-warmup).
Maria: CI run on revert branch started. Keeping this thread for notes. :eyes:
ci-bot: perf-ci: build 2951234578 (revert branch) queued
Akshay: Thanks all — will update once revert PR merges or CI gives green.
Maria: If revert doesn't land fast, we'll short-circuit routing for v5.2 to lower-traffic region to limit customer impact.
Lina: Good plan. :thumbsup:
